summary: Curated keyword-to-command map for agent discovery. Each concept lists the dedicated CLI command, when to use it, an example, related concepts and the anti-pattern (the generic fallback to avoid). The router consumes this file at runtime.

concepts.summary: Task records and local-first work items.
concepts.useWhen: You want to create, list, update or close a work item with status, priority, due date or assignee.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use `claw db tasks` or `claw collections tasks` for this. Those are fallbacks for raw schema or migration access.

concepts.summary: Notes and pages.
concepts.useWhen: You want to write, list, edit or link long-form notes and pages.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use `claw db pages` for this; the dedicated command applies the right schema and indexing.

concepts.summary: Recorded work decisions with rationale and trade-offs.
concepts.useWhen: You want to capture a non-trivial choice, its options, the selected one and why.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not store decisions as plain notes; the dedicated command keeps the structured rationale.

concepts.summary: Inbox and triage of incoming items.
concepts.useWhen: You want to drop something quickly without classifying it yet, or process the queue to promote items to tasks, notes or decisions.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not skip inbox by writing low-confidence items directly as tasks; the inbox keeps un-promoted items separate.

concepts.summary: Unified Claw projects across tasks, notes, goals and decisions.
concepts.useWhen: You want to create, list or update a project that groups related work.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use `claw db projects` for this; the dedicated command enforces the project lifecycle.

concepts.summary: Project folder manifest, attach/detach, safe handoff and path-mutable identity.
concepts.useWhen: You are inside (or pointing at) a local folder and want to attach, detach, inspect or hand off its project manifest.
concepts.antiPattern: Singular `project` is folder-level; plural `projects` is for project records. Do not confuse them.

concepts.summary: Goal records.
concepts.useWhen: You want to define, list or update higher-level goals that tasks roll up to.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not store goals as notes; the dedicated command links them to tasks and outcomes.

concepts.summary: Blockers that prevent work from progressing.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record what is blocking a task, project or decision and on whom or what it depends.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not bury blockers inside task descriptions; the dedicated command makes them queryable.

concepts.summary: Assignments of work to people, agents or teams.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record or transfer stewardship of work units explicitly.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not encode the assignee only in a task title; the dedicated command supports routing and audit.

concepts.summary: Handoffs of context, stewardship or status between agents, people or teams.
concepts.useWhen: You are passing a piece of work to someone else and want the receiving side to have the full context.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not rely on chat messages for handoffs; the dedicated command keeps the structured context.

concepts.summary: Work approvals via the signed host broker.
concepts.useWhen: You need explicit human approval for a sensitive action, transition or release.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not fake approvals as decisions; approvals require an explicit approver and broker policy.

concepts.summary: Work artifacts produced by tasks, projects or runs.
concepts.useWhen: You want to register a concrete output (file, report, build, dataset) tied to a piece of work.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not just save the file in a random folder; the dedicated command links it to its work item.

concepts.summary: Promises and follow-ups made to others or the future self.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record an explicit promise to do, deliver or check on something, separately from internal tasks.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not bury follow-up promises in chat; the dedicated command tracks deadline and party.

concepts.summary: People records.
concepts.useWhen: You want to register or look up people involved in your work and link them to tasks, assignments and handoffs.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use `claw db people` for routine lookups; the dedicated command keeps host broker forwarding for contacts.

concepts.summary: Personal work summary across tasks, projects, goals and blockers.
concepts.useWhen: You want a single read-only digest of what you currently own.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not assemble this view by hand from multiple commands; the dedicated command unifies it.

concepts.summary: Team work summary across tasks, projects, goals and blockers.
concepts.useWhen: You want a single read-only digest of what your team currently owns.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not aggregate the team view by hand; the dedicated command unifies it.

concepts.summary: Agenda view of tasks, calendar events and reminders for the current window.
concepts.useWhen: You want a single read-only view of what is happening now, today or this week.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not list tasks + calendar separately; the dedicated command unifies them.

concepts.summary: Framework calendar event records and host calendar projection.
concepts.useWhen: You want to create, list, update or delete calendar events.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use `claw db calendar_events` for this; the dedicated command projects to host calendars when broker permits.

concepts.summary: Reminders.
concepts.useWhen: You want a time-based ping at a specific moment, distinct from a calendar event.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use a task with due-date for a notify-me-at-X reminder; reminders are first-class.

concepts.summary: Deadlines.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record a hard deadline that may apply to one or many work items.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not encode deadlines only inside task fields; the dedicated command lets you query and roll-up across items.

concepts.summary: Recurring routines.
concepts.useWhen: You want to define a recurrence (daily/weekly/custom) and have it generate concrete instances.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not duplicate tasks manually for each occurrence; routines exist for this.

concepts.summary: Natural scheduling verb for placing work into time.
concepts.useWhen: You want to place an existing task or item into a specific time block or move it.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not edit calendar events to schedule tasks; the dedicated verb links them.

concepts.summary: Watch rules that monitor conditions and fire actions.
concepts.useWhen: You want to define or list a rule that watches a signal, file, query or condition and reacts when it changes.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not poll with a cron-like task; the dedicated watch surface owns the trigger lifecycle.

concepts.summary: Timeline view of work and events across time.
concepts.useWhen: You want a chronological read-only view of what happened.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not reconstruct timelines by hand from raw collections; the dedicated command unifies them.

concepts.summary: Daily and weekly review surface.
concepts.useWhen: You want to run a structured review of recent work, decisions and outcomes.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not write reviews only as notes; the dedicated command links to the underlying items.

concepts.summary: Knowledge portal backed by the private memory implementation.
concepts.useWhen: You want to capture or retrieve durable knowledge that is not a single note (concepts, references, learnings tied to topics).
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use `claw db` to look at memory; the portal applies the right scoping and redaction.

concepts.summary: Learning capture and promotion.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record a learning so the agent or team can reuse it later.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not store learnings as decisions; learnings are descriptive, decisions are prescriptive.

concepts.summary: Outcome tracking.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record what actually happened as a result of work and tie it to goals or decisions.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not conflate outcomes with tasks closed; an outcome is the realized effect, not the action.

concepts.summary: Reasoned evaluations distinct from work decisions.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record an evaluation of something (a model, a person's work, a system) without making it a decision yet.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not record judgments as decisions; judgments are inputs, decisions are commitments.

concepts.summary: Semantic planning gate.
concepts.useWhen: You want to draft, gate or revise an implementation plan before executing.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not save plans as long notes; the dedicated command gates approval and revision.

concepts.summary: Persistent agent rules.
concepts.useWhen: You want to record an explicit, persistent rule the agent should follow across sessions.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not save rules only as notes; the dedicated command makes them queryable and citable.

concepts.summary: Context packs.
concepts.useWhen: You want to bundle a reusable context (instructions + references) for an agent run.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not paste the same context into every prompt; the dedicated command lets you compose and reuse it.

concepts.summary: Reusable local skills, instructions and bundles.
concepts.useWhen: You want to manage reusable instruction bundles that agents pull on demand.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not copy-paste reusable instructions; the dedicated command versions and shares them.

concepts.summary: Compact just-in-time CLI guidance for agent and human command attempts.
concepts.useWhen: You want to surface or record short, situational hints that fire when a user or agent tries something.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use guidance to store rules; guidance is situational, rules are persistent.

concepts.summary: Keyword router that maps free-form intent to the right dedicated command.
concepts.useWhen: You do not know which command to use. Pass one or more keywords and get back commands, examples and anti-patterns.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not start exploring with `claw search query` for command discovery; `search query` is for indexed content.

concepts.summary: 30-second explanation of what Claw is for, with the capability map and the entry commands.
concepts.useWhen: You are new to the framework or want to recalibrate what Claw is for.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not skim only the README on GitHub; `claw about` reflects what is actually installed.

concepts.summary: Framework-wide search over indexed content, sources, manifests and saved searches.
concepts.useWhen: You want to find a document, note, page, surface or piece of indexed content by text.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not use `search query` to discover which command to run; use `router` for that.

concepts.summary: Read-only stable surface inspection across commands, schemas, storage, routes and contracts.
concepts.useWhen: You want the canonical registry view of commands, schemas, ADRs, surfaces or routes.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not assemble registry views by grepping source; `inspect` is the stable surface.

concepts.summary: Generic local-first database CRUD. Fallback for collections without a dedicated command and for schema or migration access.
concepts.useWhen: The thing you want has no dedicated command, or you are doing schema, migration or low-level CRUD work explicitly.
concepts.antiPattern: Do not reach for `claw db` when a dedicated command exists (tasks, notes, decisions, inbox, calendar, etc.). Use `claw router <topic>` first.
